title: alias cat='bat --paging="never"' shows "STDIN   <EMPTY>" on every ZSH prompt
body:
**What steps will reproduce the bug?**

1. alias cat to bat in ~/.zshrc
```
# use bat if bat is available
if command -v bat &>/dev/null; then
    alias cat='bat --style="header-filename,header-filesize,grid" --paging="never"'
fi
```
2. update bat version to bat 0.26.0
3. source the ~/.zshrc
4. from now of every empty prompt returns STDIN <EMPTY>


**What happens?**
After update to bat 0.26.0 every prompt show up with a STDIN <EMPTY>. I have been using the zsh configuration before and never faced any issue then
```

┏╸~────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
STDIN   <EMPTY>
Size: -
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┗╸❯❯❯ bat --version                  
bat 0.26.0
┏╸~────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
STDIN   <EMPTY>
Size: -
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: I'm using starship and don't see this problem. Does taking away the `$(gitprompt)` part of the `PROMPT` fix the problem? If so, maybe you can share more about what it does - is it a tool etc. so we can help debug?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
yes removing $(gitprompt) fixed it. 

i used https://github.com/woefe/git-prompt.zsh for the gitprompt, it is a zsh plugin

it seems be using cat in one location, may be that is the issue
https://github.com/woefe/git-prompt.zsh/blob/bd0b1d013ed9a0a0688052da69f1f62b96c09526/git-prompt.zsh#L354C9-L354C30

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> alias cat='bat --style="header-filename,header-filesize,grid" --paging="never"'

starting with bat 0.26.0 the style elements are carried over even in non-interactive terminals, see #3438

to quickly verify set, the behavior should be back to normal

```bash
alias cat='bat --decorations=never --style="header-filename,header-filesize,grid" --paging=never'
```

The problem is that you won't even see decorations in interactive terminals.

```bash
cat ...
```

A better solution would be to ask `woefe/git-prompt.zsh` to prepend `command` to `cat`, or use `\cat` to avoid alias expansion.

PS: @participant1, please revert #3438 as well

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
yeah setting `--decorations=never` fixes the issue. 

`A better solution would be to ask woefe/git-prompt.zsh to prepend command to cat, or use \cat to avoid alias expansion.` I will suggest this in that repo.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> PS: @participant1, please revert https://github.com/sharkdp/bat/pull/3438 as well

I'd rather not revert it completely because the cat compatibility fix (`bat -n | ...` ) is desired. Yes, aliasing `cat` is currently broken in some circumstances, but aliasing `cat` always comes with a risk. It would be nice to make a carefully considered fix rather than rushing.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Is there a repro command for this (can we say what call to `bat` is actually causing this)? So `bat` has been aliased to `cat`, and … something in the zsh startup script (your `.zshrc`?) contains a `cat` command? Is it possible to isolate what that is?

Or is this something that would affect *any* zsh prompt with the alias in?

**edit** I see the cat call [here](https://github.com/woefe/git-prompt.zsh/blob/bd0b1d013ed9a0a0688052da69f1f62b96c09526/git-prompt.zsh#L345-L363)

The issue is in `git-prompt.zsh` line 354 where it uses `cat` without bypassing alias expansion:

```zsh
fd_data="$(cat <&$1)"
```

This should be `command cat` to avoid picking up user aliases. @reporter has already opened a PR to fix this: woefe/git-prompt.zsh#50.

> please revert [#3438](https://github.com/sharkdp/bat/pull/3438) as well

The behavior in #3438 is correct - explicitly set styles should pipe through. This is an issue in the downstream tool, not a reason to revert.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> I'd rather not revert it completely because the cat compatibility fix (`bat -n | ...` ) is desired.

Once you set a style (e.g., in aliases, environment variables, or bat's config
file), you can no longer use bat as a reliable drop-in replacement for cat.
Decorations will always be applied to piped output unless you explicitly disable
them, which unfortunately also removes them from interactive terminals where
they are desired.

I am also against making a special case for -n, as it introduces a cascade of
inconsistencies. If -n is changed to preserve decorations in non-interactive
output, then its alias --number must behave the same way. Logically, this
extends to --style=numbers and any style combination involving it, like
--style=numbers,changes,grid.

This is precisely the complex and unpredictable behavior that was introduced in
#3438, abandoning the simple and clear rule that bat acts like cat when piped.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
If the issue is wanting configured styles to pipe like `auto` does, that's worth exploring. We'd need to understand the specific use case though. A revert doesn't address the original issues that #3438 fixed, so I think finding a solution that works for both use cases would be better.

The man page distinguishes between `style=auto` and explicitly set styles when piped here:

https://github.com/sharkdp/bat/blob/006d77fa393172b7089da27b67d3e0b235363720/doc/long-help.txt#L179

The implementation in #3438 follows this spec:
- `auto` continues to pipe as plain
- explicit styles like `-n` or `--style=numbers` are honoured

This matches how `cat -n` preserves line numbers when piped:

```sh
$ echo "hello" | cat -n | wc -c
13
$ echo "hello" | bat -n | wc -c    # was 6, now 11
```

The [earlier discussion](https://github.com/sharkdp/bat/pull/3438#issuecomment-3418199723) covered the technical rationale and referenced the multiple issues requesting this behaviour.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
The comparison to `cat -n` isn’t entirely accurate. The tool is plain by
default, while `bat` displays decorations in the terminal but omits them for
non-interactive ones. My decision to customize the appearance with `--style`
should not override this fundamental behavior, as it creates the unexpected
pitfall described by OP.

If a full revert isn’t wanted, I should be able to control this behavior when
setting a style. For example:

```bash
# Currently includes decorations when piped, which is unexpected
seq 5 | bat --style=numbers,changes,grid | cat

# => Should have NO decorations
seq 5 | bat --style=numbers,changes,grid,auto | cat

# => Should have NO decorations
seq 5 | bat --style=numbers,changes,grid --decorations=auto | cat
```

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
> `seq 5 | bat --style=numbers,changes,grid,auto | cat`

Huh, I had never thought to put auto along with other styles like that 🤔 

An alternative idea that brings to mind is to perhaps instead add `auto` to the style sequence to reinstate auto-like piping?

- Would avoid having to set a whole new flag, possibly easier to understand.
- goes from "if style **is** auto then no pipe" to "if style **includes** auto then no pipe".

So someone could say `bat --style=numbers,auto` and have it not pipe with them.

**edit** - on re-reading I think that is actually what you are proposing? Can you clarify exactly what you are suggesting the change is?

I presume decorations is already set to auto by default so adding `--decorations=auto` would not have any effect on the actual value internally.

Maybe there are downsides to this I am not thinking of though 🤔 

This warrants a fresh issue though to avoid treading on the toes of this one
